fact_types.title: Are you a married taxpayer whose filing status is married filing separately or head of household (2025 Form 1040 instructions, line 27a, Step 3 question 3)? Under Head of Household in those instructions, an interlocutory decree still means you are married, and a final decree of divorce or of separate maintenance at the end of 2025 means you are considered unmarried. Publication 596, Rule 3, still treats you as married when you file as head of household under the special rules for married taxpayers living apart, including when you lived apart and are considered unmarried for head of household. Yes continues to the separated-spouse questions. No skips questions 4 and 5 and continues to question 6. Asked of a head of household with a qualifying child, including one who already answered the separated-spouse question no. Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default, presence-before-value, free supersession.

Second selection path required by rule-artifact.v14 selection.paths minItems 2. Nothing asks this fact. Every value is refused at assertion, so a stored value cannot activate the path, change line 27a, or refuse together with a separated-spouse answer. Not an input question.
